Consumer Non-Cyclicals: The Consumer Non‑Cyclicals sector topped the 15‑sector ranking, driven by the strongest median price gain over the past 30 days. Six of the ten listed companies posted positive price moves, pulling the sector’s median well above the SGX overall average. Robust consumer confidence, a rebound in tourism spending, stable Singapore dollar rates, recent regulatory incentives for retail firms, and favourable commodity cost dynamics are all factors uniquely shaping the sector’s health. These conditions have likely boosted earnings expectations and investor sentiment, explaining the sector’s outperformance. With a leading rank and a majority of stocks in the green, the sector appears to be in solid short‑term momentum.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector, with 84 listed companies, ranked 7th out of 15 in median price change over the past 30 days, outpacing the overall SGX median. Only 17 of the 84 firms posted a positive price change in the same period, yet the sector’s aggregate momentum remained strong. This outperformance is likely driven by robust consumer spending, a rebound in regional tourism, a stable interest‑rate environment, resilient supply‑chain conditions, and favorable exchange‑rate dynamics that uniquely support the Consumer Cyclicals market health in the Singapore index.
Transportation & Logistics: The Transportation & Logistics sector lagged behind most peers, slipping to 13th place out of 15 based on median price changes over the past 30 days. Its median price movement was below the overall SGX median, and only one of the eight listed companies posted a positive return in the same period. This underperformance likely reflects a confluence of headwinds such as rising fuel costs, tighter emissions regulations, regional trade tensions, port capacity constraints and labour shortages that are uniquely pressing for Singapore’s logistics network. With just a single stock showing gains, the sector’s breadth of weakness underscores the broader pressure on freight volumes and shipping rates. These market‑specific factors together help explain why the sector’s price momentum has been notably weaker than the broader market.
Healthcare: The Healthcare sector, with 40 listed companies, slipped to 10th place out of 15 in the 30‑day median price‑change ranking, indicating a weaker performance than the SGX overall median. Only 10 of the 40 firms recorded a positive price change over the same period, underscoring the breadth of the decline. This under‑performance may be tied to tighter regulatory scrutiny, adjustments in government reimbursement policies, an aging local population altering demand patterns, a slowdown in global biotech funding, and ongoing supply‑chain disruptions that uniquely affect Singapore’s healthcare market.
Properties & Real Estate: The Properties & Real Estate sector lagged behind the broader market, posting a median price decline that placed it ninth out of fifteen sectors based on the last 30 days of price changes. Out of the 53 listed companies, only ten recorded a positive price move during the same period, highlighting the breadth of the weakness. Elevated financing costs, tighter loan‑to‑value limits, recent regulatory cooling measures, rising construction material prices, and a slowdown in both domestic and foreign demand are likely contributors to the sector’s under‑performance relative to the SGX overall median.
Energy: The Energy sector, comprising 23 listed companies, slipped to 11th place out of 15 in the 30‑day median price‑change ranking, with its median price movement trailing the overall SGX median. Only five of the 23 firms recorded a positive price change over the period, underscoring the breadth of the decline. Weak demand for fossil fuels, higher input costs and tighter emissions regulations are likely weighing on the sector, while global oil price volatility, regional carbon‑tax policy, supply‑chain constraints and an accelerating shift toward renewable energy are current factors uniquely affecting the health of the Energy market in the Singapore index.
Utilities: The Utilities sector, comprising 13 listed companies, slipped to 8th place out of 15 in the median price‑change ranking over the past month. Its median price change lagged behind the overall SGX median, and only three of the 13 constituents posted a positive price move in the same period. The weaker performance likely reflects heightened input‑cost pressures and ongoing regulatory reviews of electricity tariffs, which have dampened investor sentiment. Factors uniquely influencing the Singapore Utilities market today include fuel price volatility, pending tariff reforms, the transition toward renewable generation, water resource constraints, and grid reliability concerns.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector, comprising 30 listed companies, ranked fifth among fifteen sectors for median price change over the past month, outpacing the overall SGX median movement. Ten of the thirty constituents posted positive price changes, underscoring the sector’s relative strength. Robust demand for essential goods, low price elasticity and a generally stable consumer base appear to have driven the outperformance. Current market conditions that can uniquely affect the sector’s health in the Singapore index include regional tourism recovery, commodity price stability, currency fluctuations, and government stimulus aimed at household consumption.
Financial Services: The Financial Services sector, made up of 29 listed firms, ranked fourth out of fifteen sectors for median price change over the past 30 days, outpacing the broader SGX market. Eight companies posted positive price moves while the remaining peers recorded declines, indicating that a minority of strong performers lifted the sector’s median. This outperformance likely reflects solid earnings from loan growth and fee‑based services, bolstered by a supportive monetary policy stance and relatively stable interest‑rate expectations. Current market health is also shaped by regional banking stress, ongoing regulatory reforms, capital‑flow dynamics, and macroeconomic stability in Singapore.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector lagged sharply, ranking 14th out of 15 based on median price changes over the past 30 days. Only one of its 15 constituents posted a positive price move, leaving the median change well below the overall SGX median. The under‑performance likely reflects a squeeze on advertising spend, tighter content‑licensing regulations, rising interest rates that increase financing costs for telecom operators, and intensified competition from over‑the‑top streaming platforms, all of which uniquely pressure the Singapore Communication Services market.
Basic Materials: Ranking third among fifteen SGX sectors, the Basic Materials group posted the strongest median price gain over the recent 30‑day window, outpacing the overall market. With 36 constituents, only a third (12) posted positive returns, yet the median uplift was enough to lift the sector ahead of peers, suggesting that the gains were driven by a subset of larger‑cap players pulling the median upward. This performance may reflect tighter global commodity supplies, rising regional construction activity, recent regulatory reviews of mining licences, currency fluctuations, and supply‑chain disruptions, all of which uniquely affect the Basic Materials market health in the Singapore index.
Infrastructures: Ranking second among fifteen SGX sectors, the Infrastructures segment posted the strongest median price gain over the past month, with four of its seven constituents posting positive returns. The sector’s outperformance relative to the broader market likely reflects heightened government capital projects and renewed focus on sustainable urban development, which have boosted investor sentiment toward infrastructure assets. Additional drivers include favourable financing conditions, increased regional logistics demand, and recent regulatory incentives for green construction.
REIT: Out of 15 sectors, the REIT sector ranked sixth based on median price change over the past month, and it outperformed the broader SGX index in the same period. Of the 38 REITs tracked, 13 posted positive price moves, indicating that just under a third are driving the sector’s gain. The stronger performance could be linked to lower financing costs, robust rental demand, a supportive regulatory environment, limited new supply, and steady foreign investor appetite, all of which uniquely influence Singapore’s REIT market health. These factors together help explain why the sector’s median price change exceeded the market average despite a modest share of winners.
Industrials: Despite comprising 126 firms, the Industrials sector lagged behind most peers, slipping to 12th out of 15 in the 30‑day median price‑change ranking. Only 23 companies posted gains, while the sector’s median move fell short of the SGX overall median, reflecting weaker investor sentiment. The underperformance may stem from tightened credit conditions, lingering global supply‑chain bottlenecks, subdued domestic infrastructure orders, recent regulatory tightening on heavy‑equipment imports, higher borrowing costs, and volatile exchange rates. These factors together pressure earnings outlook for Singapore‑listed industrials.
Technology: The Technology sector, made up of 57 listed firms, placed 15th out of 15 in the sector ranking based on median price changes over the past 30 days, indicating the weakest momentum among all SGX sectors. Its median price change lagged behind the overall SGX median, and only 10 of the 57 companies posted a positive price movement in the same period. This underperformance likely reflects subdued corporate IT spending, delayed rollout of new hardware projects, and intensified competition from regional peers. At the same time, Singapore‑specific factors such as tighter monetary policy, a stronger local currency, recent regulatory tightening on data‑center approvals, and supply‑chain constraints for semiconductor components are uniquely pressuring the technology market health.
